newsitem.title: CHINA: Inflation falls in China's remote Tibet region.
newsitem.headline: Inflation falls in China's remote Tibet region.

text.p: China's tight monetary policy helped to slash retail price inflation in the remote Himalayan region of Tibet to 7.2 percent in 1996, down 10.2 percentage points from the year before, the Tibet Daily said.

Retail price inflation dropped to 7.2 percent in 1996 from 17.4 percent in 1995 and consumer price inflation decreased to 7.8 percent in 1996 from 19.4 percent in 1995, it said in an edition seen in Beijing on Wednesday.
The lower inflation rate was attributed to China's tight monetary policy and greater attention on controlling inflation by party and government departments at all levels, it said.
